warnings.text:
Marine Works - Diving Operations - Vancouver Harbour
Diving Operations East of Second Narrows, on the South side of the channel near the FRPD McKenzie derrick in the vicinity of 49 17.650N 123 01.155W.
Hours of Operation;
Day 1, 30 Oct 2026 2330 UTC to 31 Oct 2026 0330 UTC,
Day 2, 31 Oct 2026 2345 UTC to 01 Nov 2026 0500 UTC,
Day 3, 02 Nov 2026 0130 UTC to 02 Nov 2026 0630 UTC,
Day 4, 03 Nov 2026 0300 UTC to 03 Nov 2026 0830 UTC.
Mariner requested to detour North a minimum of 100 meters.
During active diving operations, the following vessel traffic measures will apply:
 - 100 metres separation is required from the dive operation.
 - Light tugs and commercial vessels may be permitted to transit on the north side of the channel at a slow but safe speed, provided the required separation can be maintained.
   - Should your tier 2 vessel require a lift of the Second Narrows Rail Bridge, it should be entered into the Centralized Scheduling System.
- Tier 1 vessels and tug & barges will be unable to transit during the times posted above. Please plan your transits around these scheduled times.

FOR THE EXERCISE AREA LOCATED WITHIN INTERNATIONAL WATERS AND 
AIRSPACE OF AEGEAN SEA REGARDING THE TURKISH NAVY AND AIRFORCE A 
FIRING MILITARY EXERCISE (ASFAO) TO BE CONDUCTED 02 NOV 0600-31 DEC 
1300 UTC WITH 200903 LTAAYNYX OCT 2026. 
 
2. GREEK AIS DID NOT PROMULGATE APPROPRIATE NOTAM FOR THE EXERCISE 
AREA IN ACCORDANCE WITH OUR REF MESSAGE 200903 LTAAYNYX OCT 2026. 
UNDER THESE CIRCUMSTANCES DUE TO THE INSISTENT ATTITUDE OF GREECE, 
TURKIYE IS LEFT WITH NO OTHER ALTERNATIVE BUT TO TAKE ITS OWN 
INITATIVE TO PROMULGATE THE NECESSARY NOTAM FOR THE EXERCISE AREA. 
 
TURKIYE WILL TAKE NECESSARY MEASURES FOR THE SAFETY OF THE GENERAL 
AIR TRAFFIC AS SHE DID IN THE PAST AND IS ALWAYS READY FOR 
COOPERATION AND COORDINATION IN THIS RESPECT.

Routeing Change - North Atlantic Right Whale - Maritimes, Newfoundland, St. Lawrence
warnings.text:
Routeing Change - North Atlantic Right Whale - Maritimes, Newfoundland, St. Lawrence
Effective 241500 UTC Oct 2026, the following North Atlantic Right Whale restriction Zones are in effect for all vessels greater than 13 meters in length overall:
Static Zones North and South: Vessels must not exceed 10 knots over ground.
Dynamic Shipping Zones A, B, C, D, and E: No restriction in effect.
Seasonal Management Areas 1 and 2: No restriction in effect.
Restricted area: No restriction in effect.
Voluntary Seasonal Slowdown: Vessels are requested to reduce their speed less than 10 knots over ground.
Additional details are available in Notices to Mariners. Failure to comply with speed restrictions in effect can lead to enforcement action by Transport Canada.
Mariners are requested to report whale sightings and observations of entangled, dead, or injured whales to Marine Communication and Traffic Services.
                                                    Cancels NW-C-4464-26

warnings.subject: Marine Works - Bridge Repair - Richelieu River and Northern Lake Champlain - Turcotte Bridge
warnings.text:
Marine Works - Bridge Repair - Richelieu River and Northern Lake Champlain - Turcotte Bridge
Repair work taking place daily, 24 hours a day at the Turcotte Bridge. Barge and tug on scene. Navigation channel reduced to 21.5 metres and is marked and lit. Air draft reduced to 12 metres.
Any vessels requiring the barge be moved to make passage under the bridge are required to give 72 hours notice by e-mailing m.poirier@pomerleau.ca or alexis.noel@pomerleau.ca, and provide them with:
Date and time of requested passage, vessel name and type, estimated speed of passage, length, beam, and draft of the vessel, and their contact information.
All vessels transiting the area are requested to remain 3 metres away from the barge.
Minimum wake requested.

warnings.subject: NAVIGATIONAL WARNING TO ALL CONCERNED:
warnings.text:
A3696/26 NOTAMN Q) LGGG/QAFXX/IV/NBO/E /000/999/3705N02445E341 A) LGGG  PART 1 OF 3  B) 2610112100  C) 2611112059  E) NAVIGATIONAL WARNING TO ALL CONCERNED: 
REF (A) GREEK NOTAM A3635/26 (021116 EUECYIYN OCT 2026). 
REF (B) TURKISH NOTAM A4496/26 (051728 EUECYIYN OCT 2026). 
WITH REFERENCE TO REF (B) TURKISH NOTAM A4496/26 WE POINT OUT THAT 
THE ASSERTIONS CONTAINED THEREIN ARE REJECTED AS MISLEADING AND 
DEVOID OF ANY LEGAL BASIS. IN THIS RESPECT AND FURTHER TO THE REF 
(A) GREEK NOTAM A3635/26, PARA 2.2, WE REITERATE THAT GREECE, 
ESTABLISHED IN 1931 IN ACCORDANCE WITH INTERNATIONAL LAW A 
TERRITORIAL SEA OF TEN NAUTICAL MILES FOR THE PURPOSES OF AVIATION 
AND THE CONTROL THEREOF. 
THEREFORE, GREEK AIRSPACE DOES NOT EXCEED THE BREADTH OF THE 
TERRITORIAL SEA AS ESTABLISHED IN 1931. 
GREECE, THEREFORE, FULLY ABIDES BY INTERNATIONAL LAW AND WILL 
CONTINUE TO DO SO WHILE FULLY EXERCISING ITS SOVEREIGNTY. IN FACT, AS 
FAR AS INTERNATIONAL LAW IS CONCERNED, TURKIYE IS THE ONLY COUNTRY, 
REGRETTABLY, WHICH ALSO FAILS TO RESPECT THE PROVISIONS OF THE 
CHICAGO CONVENTION WITHIN THE ATHINAI FIR, WHERE, IN ACCORDANCE WITH 
THE ICAO REGIONAL AIR NAVIGATION AGREEMENTS OF 1950-1952-1958, THE 
GREEK AUTHORITIES ARE THE ONLY COMPETENT AUTHORITIES CHARGED TO 
IMPLEMENT THE RELEVANT PROVISIONS OF THE CHICAGO END PART 1 OF 3
A3696/26 NOTAMN Q) LGGG/QAFXX/IV/NBO/E /000/999/3705N02445E341 A) LGGG  PART 2 OF 3  B) 2610112100  C) 2611112059  E) CONVENTION AND TO 
ENSURE UNIMPEDED, REGULAR AND SAFE AIR TRAFFIC. 
ALSO, REFERENCE IS MADE TO THE ABOVE REF (B) TURKISH NOTAM A4496/26 
IN ORDER TO STATE THAT THE ATHINAI/ISTANBUL FIR BOUNDARY BETWEEN 
POINTS 404500N0261000E AND 360500N0300000E HAS BEEN ESTABLISHED BY 
ICAO REGIONAL AGREEMENTS (REACHED IN THE SECOND MIDDLE EAST REGIONAL AIR NAVIGATION MEETING, ISTANBUL 1950 AND SUBSEQUENTLY APPROVED BY 
THE ICAO COUNCIL ON 14 DEC 1950, DOC 7055 MID/2-RAC) WITH THE 
PARTICIPATION AND APPROVAL OF TURKIYE AND IN FEB 1958, (DOC 7870, 
EUM/IV) AND CONSEQUENTLY IS FOUNDED ON THE FIRMEST POSSIBLE LEGAL 
BASIS AS NOTED IN OUR A1709/07 LGGGYNYX NOTAM. 
FURTHERMORE THE SAID ATHINAI/ISTANBUL FIR BOUNDARY WAS DEPICTED ON 
CHART NUMBER 7 ATTACHED TO THE REGIONAL AIR NAVIGATION AGREEMENT 
WHICH WAS REACHED IN THE THIRD REGIONAL AIR NAVIGATIONAL CONFERENCE 
(PARIS 1952) AND SUBSEQUENTLY APPROVED BY THE ICAO COUNCIL ON 23 
JUNE 1952. 
ACCORDINGLY, GREECE HAS BEEN ASIGNED RESPONSIBILITY FOR ALL ATM 
SERVICES AND ICAO PURPOSES AS WELL AS FOR SAR WITHIN 
ATHINAI FIR/ HELLAS UIR AND IS THE ONLY COMPETENT THEREIN. 
FINALLY, THE ADDITIONAL PROVISION MENTIONED IN PARAGRAPH 2.3 OF 
THE REF (A) GREEK END PART 2 OF 3
A3696/26 NOTAMN Q) LGGG/QAFXX/IV/NBO/E /000/999/3705N02445E341 A) LGGG  PART 3 OF 3  B) 2610112100  C) 2611112059  E) NOTAM A3635/26 (021116 EUECYIYN OCT 2026) AIM AT 
THE PROMOTION OF SAFETY, REGULARITY AND EFFICIENCY OF INTERNATIONAL 
AIR NAVIGATION AND FOR UNMANNED AIRCRAFT IDENTIFICATION PURPOSES IN 
CONFORMITY WITH ARTICLE 3 (D) OF THE ICAO CONVENTION ON INTERNATIONAL 
CIVIL AVIATION AS AMPLIFIED BY THE A40-04 ICAO ASSEMBLY RESOLUTIONS, 
APPENDIX I, RESOLVING CLAUSE 2, SEE ALSO THE ANNEX 2, APPENDIX 4, TO 
THE ICAO CONVENTION ON INTERNATIONAL CIVIL AVIATION AS WELL AS 
ARTICLE 12 OF THE ICAO CONVENTION AND THE ESTABLISHED INTERNATIONAL 
PRACTICE. 
CONSEQUENTLY, THE POINTS RAISED BY TURKIYE IN REF (B) TURKISH NOTAM 
A4496/26 (051728 EUECYIYN OCT 2026), ARE IRRELEVANT AND THE SAID NOTAM IS NULL AND VOID AND NOT APPLICABLE TO ATHINAI FIR/ HELLAS 
UIR. THE REQUIREMENTS EXPRESSED IN THE REF (A) GREEK NOTAM 
A3635/26, ARE FULLY IN FORCE. END PART 3 OF 3

E)AS A RESPONSE MEASURE TO THE DECISION OF THE MALTESE AVIATION
AUTHORITIES STIPULATING THAT ALL AIRCRAFT OWNED, CHARTERED OR
OPERATED, OR OTHERWISE CONTROLLED BY CITIZENS OF THE RUSSIAN
FEDERATION AND ALL OPERATORS HOLDING AIR OPERATOR CERTIFICATE (AOC)
ISSUED BY THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION AUTHORITIES ARE PROHIBITED FROM
TAKING OFF, LANDING OR OVERFLYING THE TERRITORY OF THE REPUBLIC OF
MALTA, AS PER NOTAM A1873/26, THE AVIATION AUTHORITIES OF THE
RUSSIAN FEDERATION HEREBY INFORM THAT ALL AIRCRAFT OWNED, CHARTERED
OR OPERATED, OR OTHERWISE CONTROLLED BY CITIZENS OF THE REPUBLIC OF
MALTA, AND ALL OPERATORS HOLDING AOC ISSUED BY MALTESE AUTHORITIES,
AND AIRCRAFT REGISTERED IN MALTA, ARE PROHIBITED FROM TAKING OFF,
LANDING OR OVERFLYING THE TERRITORY OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION,
EXCEPT FOR HUMANITARIAN, SAR FLIGHTS, EMERGENCY LANDING OR
EMERGENCY OVERFLIGHT, AND CASES WHEN A SPECIAL PERMISSION FOR
FLIGHT OPERATIONS IS GRANTED BY THE FEDERAL AIR TRANSPORT AGENCY OR
THE MINISTRY OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION AS
APPROPRIATE.

warnings.subject: UKRAINIAN CRISIS:
warnings.text:
A1134/26 NOTAMR A0766/26
Q)LBSR/QAFXX/IV/NBO/E/000/999/4252N02627E195
A)LBSR
B)2609280800 C)2612162359EST
E)UKRAINIAN CRISIS:
IT SHALL BE PROHIBITED FOR ANY ACFT OPERATED BY RUSSIAN AIR 
CARRIERS, OR FOR ANY RUSSIAN REGISTERED ACFT, OR FOR ANY NON-
RUSSIAN-REGISTERED ACFT WHICH IS OWNED OR CHARTERED, OR OTHERWISE 
CONTROLLED BY ANY RUSSIAN NATURAL OR LEGAL PERSON, ENTITY OR BODY, 
TO LAND IN, TAKE-OFF FROM OR OVERFLY THE TERRITORY OF THE REPUBLIC 
OF BULGARIA.
THE PROHIBITITION SHALL NOT APPLY IN THE CASE OF AN EMERGENCY 
LANDING OR AN EMERGENCY OVERFLIGHT AND TO ACFT THAT HAVE A MAXIMUM 
SEATING CAPACITY OF 4 PERSONS AND A MAXIMUM TAKE-OFF MASS OF NO MORE 
THAN 2000KG WHEN USED FOR PRIVATE, NON-CORPORATE, FLIGHTS FOR 
RECREATIONAL PURPOSES OR FOR THE PURPOSE OF TRAINING FOR PRIVATE 
PILOT LICENSES AND RELATED RATINGS WITH UNION TRAINING PROVIDERS.

3. SPECIAL RESTRICTIONS 
NO FLIGHT OPERATIONS SHALL BE PERMITTED EXCEPT COMMERCIAL FLIGHTS 
(NOTE 1), BUSINESS FLIGHTS (NOTE 2), AND FLIGHTS FOR MILITARY, 
CUSTOMS, POLICE SERVICES, AND FIRE-FIGHTING RESCUE PURPOSES. 
4. OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS 
4.1 MANNED AIRCRAFT SHALL BE EQUIPPED WITH A SECONDARY 
SURVEILLANCE RADAR (SSR) TRANSPONDER OR OTHER SURVEILLANCE 
EQUIPMENT OF EQUIVALENT PERFORMANCE, WHICH SHALL REMAIN ACTIVATED 
THROUGHOUT THE FLIGHT. UNMANNED AIRCRAFT SHALL HAVE RELIABLE 
SURVEILLANCE CAPABILITY, FITTED WITH AN AIRBORNE OPERATIONAL 
IDENTIFICATION TRANSMITTING MODULE, AN SSR TRANSPONDER OR 
SURVEILLANCE EQUIPMENT OF EQUIVALENT 
F)SFC G)UNL) 
// // PERFORMANCE, WHICH SHALL REMAIN ACTIVATED THROUGHOUT THE 
FLIGHT. 
4.2 PILOTS SHALL MAINTAIN CONTINUOUS TWO-WAY COMMUNICATION WITH 
AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL (ATC) UNIT. REMOTE PILOTS OF UNMANNED AIRCRAFT 
SYSTEM END PART 1 OF 3
A4484/26 NOTAMN Q) ZXXX/QXXXX/IV/NBO/W/000/999/3954N11623E162 A) ZBPE ZYSH ZSHA  PART 2 OF 3  B) 2609191600  C) PERM  E) (UAS) SHALL HAVE RELIABLE MEANS FOR TWO-WAY COMMUNICATION 
WITH ATC UNIT. IN THE EVENT OF LOSS OF TWO-WAY COMMUNICATION, 
PILOTS OR REMOTE PILOTS OF UAS SHALL IMMEDIATELY SET THE SSR 
TRANSPONDER CODE FOR RADIO COMMUNICATION FAILURE, AND TAKE ALL 
FEASIBLE MEASURES TO OBTAIN ACKNOWLEDGEMENT FROM ATC UNIT. 
4.3 PRIOR TO ENTERING THE SPECIAL RESTRICTED AREA, AIRCRAFT MUST 
REPORT THEIR SECURITY STATUS (NOTE 3) TO THE ATC UNIT AND 
COOPERATE WITH AIRBORNE TARGET RECOGNITION. WHEN NECESSARY, 
AIRCRAFT WITHIN THE SPECIAL RESTRICTED AREA SHALL BE SUBJECT TO 
AIRBORNE SECURITY VERIFICATION. 
4.4 AIRCRAFT SHALL OPERATE STRICTLY IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE 
APPROVED FLIGHT PLAN. ANY INTENTION OR ACTION TO DEVIATE FROM THE 
FLIGHT PLAN MUST BE REPORTED TO ATC UNIT IN A 
F)SFC G)UNL) 
// // TIMELY MANNER AND APPROVED PRIOR TO EXECUTION. 
4.5 WHEN CIVIL AIRCRAFT OPERATES BELOW 3,000M (INCLUDED) ABOVE 
MEAN SEA LEVEL, THE INDICATED AIRSPEED (IAS) SHOULD NOT EXCEED 
450KMH.

warnings.text:
U1174/26 NOTAMR U0725/26
Q)UUWV/QOAXX/IV/BO/A/000/999/5535N03716E999
A)UUUU B)2609010630 C)2612012359 EST
E)AS A RESPONSE MEASURE TO THE DECISION OF THE AVIATION AUTHORITIES
OF FINLAND STIPULATING THAT ALL ACFT OWNED, CHARTERED OR OPERATED,
OR OTHERWISE CONTROLLED BY CITIZENS OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION AND
ALL OPERATORS HOLDING AIR OPERATOR CERTIFICATE (AOC) ISSUED BY THE
RUSSIAN FEDERATION AUTHORITIES ARE PROHIBITED FROM TAKE-OFF,
LANDING OR OVERFLYING FINLAND, AIP SUP 022/2024, THE AVIATION
AUTHORITIES OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION HEREBY INFORM THAT ALL
AIRCRAFT OWNED, CHARTERED OR OPERATED, OR OTHERWISE CONTROLLED BY
CITIZENS OF FINLAND ARE PROHIBITED FROM OVERFLYING THE AIRSPACE OF
THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION, EXCEPT FOR EMERGENCY, HUM, SAR, MEDICAL
FLIGHTS AND ACFT WITH PERMISSION FOR FLIGHTS GRANTED BY THE FEDERAL
AIR TRANSPORT AGENCY OR THE MINISTRY OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS OF THE
RUSSIAN FEDERATION, AS APPROPRIATE.

CHARTERED, OPERATED OR OTHERWISE CONTROLLED BY CITIZENS OF THE
RUSSIAN FEDERATION AND BY OPERATORS HOLDING AIR OPERATOR
CERTIFICATE (AOC) ISSUED BY THE AUTHORITIES OF THE RUSSIAN
FEDERATION ARE PROHIBITED FROM ENTERING, EXITING OR OVERFLYING THE
AIRSPACE OF CYPRUS (REF AIP SUP 001/2024), THE AVIATION AUTHORITIES
OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION HEREBY INFORM THAT ALL AIRCRAFT OWNED,
CHARTERED, OPERATED OR OTHERWISE CONTROLLED BY CITIZENS OF CYPRUS
 AND BY OPERATORS HOLDING AOC ISSUED BY THE AUTHORITIES OF THE
 REPUBLIC OF CYPRUS ARE PROHIBITED FROM ENTERING, EXITING OR
 OVERFLYING THE AIRSPACE OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION EXCEPT FOR
 AIRCRAFT IN AN EMERGENCY, HUMANITARIAN FLIGHTS, AMBULANCE FLIGHTS
 AND IN CASES WHEN A SPECIAL PERMISSION FOR FLIGHT OPERATIONS IS
 GRANTED BY THE FEDERAL AIR TRANSPORT AGENCY OR THE MINISTRY OF
 FOREIGN AFFAIRS OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION AS APPROPRIATE.

warnings.subject: Waterway information - ECHO Program - Haro Strait, Strait of Georgia, Washington State - San Juan Islands
warnings.text:
Waterway information - ECHO Program - Haro Strait, Strait of Georgia, Washington State - San Juan Islands
HARO STRAIT AND BOUNDARY PASS – ECHO Program 2025 Voluntary Ship Slowdown 
Effective June 15 to November 30, 2026 the ECHO Program voluntary ship slowdown through Haro Strait and Boundary Pass is active for all inbound and outbound commercial and government vessels to reduce underwater noise for at-risk whales. This initiative will remain in effect 24 hours per day until 2359 PDT on November 30, 2026, depending on southern resident killer whale presence in the fall. If it is safe and operationally feasible to do so, commercial and government vessels are requested to not exceed the following speeds through the water: 
11 knots – Bulkers, tankers, general cargo vessels, and government vessels; and, 
14.5 knots – Vehicle carriers, cruise ships, and container vessels. 
This voluntary slowdown takes place between the vessel traffic separation scheme at the south end of Haro Strait at 48-24-22.78 N ,123-12-15.26 W, and the vessel traffic separation scheme at the north end of Boundary Pass at 48-46-39.28 N, 123-1-36.84 W. There are also two optional slow down areas, one rounding Turn Point and the other between Saturna Island and Alden Point, Patos Island. 
The ECHO Program is led by the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority in collaboration with government agencies, Indigenous communities, industry partners and environmental groups.  
For more detailed information, refer to the following internet web address: 
https://www.portvancouver.com/echo/

warnings.subject: Juan de Fuca Voluntary Lateral Displacement - Juan de Fuca Strait
warnings.text:
Juan de Fuca Voluntary Lateral Displacement - Juan de Fuca Strait
Effective June 1 to October 31, 2026, the ECHO Program voluntary route alteration is active for all tugs transiting the Canadian inshore area of the Strait of Juan de Fuca to reduce underwater noise for at-risk whales.  
If it is safe and operationally feasible to do so, tugs are requested to navigate either through the outbound shipping lane or the inshore route alteration zone, while maintaining a buffer distance of 1,000 meters from the traffic separation scheme (TSS). The inshore route alteration zone is 1,500 meters wide and occurs between 123-52-21.192 W, 48-18-37.332 N and 124-31-33.378 W, 48-28-53.316 N, covering approximately 28 NM.  
The ECHO Program is led by the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority in collaboration with government agencies, Indigenous communities, industry partners and environmental groups. 
For more detailed information, refer to the following internet web address: 
https://www.portvancouver.com/echo/

warnings.subject: Swiftsure Bank Voluntary Slowdown - Juan de Fuca Strait, Pacific South Coast, West Coast Vancouver Island South
warnings.text:
Swiftsure Bank Voluntary Slowdown - Juan de Fuca Strait, Pacific South Coast, West Coast Vancouver Island South
Effective June 1 to October 31, 2026, the ECHO Program voluntary ship slowdown in the vicinity of Swiftsure Bank is active for all inbound and outbound commercial and government vessels to reduce underwater noise for at-risk whales.  If it is safe and operationally feasible to do so, commercial and government vessels are requested to not exceed the following speeds through the water: 
11 knots – Bulkers, tankers, general cargo vessels, and government vessels; and, 
14.5 knots – Vehicle carriers, cruise ships, and container vessels. 
The voluntary ship slowdown takes place at Swiftsure Bank between 125° 17' W or 48° 19' N on the western or southern sides, and 124° 40’ W on the eastern side. All vessels transiting inbound or outbound are asked to slowdown when it is safe and operationally feasible to do so. Speed transition zones are in place about 2 nautical miles prior to entering the slowdown area. 
The ECHO Program is led by the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority in collaboration with government agencies, Indigenous communities, industry partners and environmental groups. 
For more detailed information, refer to the following internet web address: 
https://www.portvancouver.com/echo/

warnings.subject: Waterway information - Strait of Georgia, West Coast Vancouver Island South
warnings.text:
Waterway information - Strait of Georgia, West Coast Vancouver Island South
Effective 0700 UTC JUN 1 2026, to comply with the Interim Order for the Protection of Southern Resident Killer Whales (Orcinus orca) in the Waters of Southern British Columbia, 2026, vessels must not approach within a distance of 1000m of a Southern Resident Killer Whale in the Southern Resident Killer Whale critical habitat and British Columbia coastal waters east of Vancouver Island and south of Campbell River (Cape Mudge) and Ucluelet, including Barkley Sound (up to Port Alberni) and Howe Sound, with coordinates listed in Schedule 1 of the Interim Order.
These prohibitions are in effect until May 31st, 2027. Details of vessel exceptions from the approach distance are described in Sections 2(1), 2(2), 3(2), and 4(2) of the Interim Order. Note that vessels in transit are excepted from the approach distance measure.
Vessels must not operate or navigate within the two Vessel Restricted Zones, specifically those waters off the eastern coast of Saturna Island and southern coast of North Pender Island, with the coordinates listed in Schedule 2 of the Interim Order.
The Vessel Restricted Zones are in effect until November 30th, 2026. Details of vessel exceptions from the Vessel Restricted Zone prohibitions are described in Sections 2(1), 2(2), 5(2) and 6(2) of the Interim Order.
In addition, vessels must adhere to the requirements of two Speed Restricted Zones near Swiftsure Bank, in which all vessels are restricted to a maximum speed of 10 knots over ground, with the coordinates listed in Schedule 3 of the Interim Order.
The Speed Restricted Zones are in effect until November 30th, 2026. Details of vessel exceptions from the Speed Restricted Zones are described in Sections 2(1), 2(2), 7(2) and 8(2) of the Interim Order.
Failure to comply with the Interim Order for the Protection of the Southern Resident Killer Whales in the Waters of Southern British Columbia, 2026 could lead to enforcement action, including fines.
Further details are available at Transport Canada’s website (Interim Order for the Protection of the Southern Resident Killer Whale (Orcinus orca) in the Waters of Southern British Columbia, 2026 (canada.ca), or upon request from a Marine Communications and Traffic Services Centre.

warnings.subject: Waterway information - Calculation of under-keel clearance - Montréal to Trois-Rivières
warnings.text:
Waterway information - Calculation of under-keel clearance - Montréal to Trois-Rivières
Canadian Coast Guard Marine Communications and Traffic Services have been using all Canadian Hydrographic Service water-level stations for the calculation of passage authorizations in the SorelMontreal sector of the navigational waterway, namely Sorel, Contrecoeur, Varennes, Montreal-Frontenac and Montreal-Jetty No. 1.
In light of the particular features of the navigational waterway in the portion between buoys M84 (downstream of the municipality of Verchères) and M11 (downstream of the Bellmouth curve), it was agreed to adjust upward the available water column by 10 cm in this portion.
The minimum water column in this portion of the navigational waterway as per the Contrecur hydrographic station, obtained after adjustment, will be used for the calculation of under-keel clearance.
                                                    Cancels NW-Q-1491-22

warnings.subject: Waterway information - Calculation of under-keel clearance - Montréal to Trois-Rivières - Montréal-Est to Verchères
warnings.text:
Waterway information - Calculation of under-keel clearance - Montréal to Trois-Rivières - Montréal-Est to Verchères
Canadian Coast Guard Marine Communications and Traffic Services have been using all Canadian Hydrographic Service water-level stations for the calculation of passage authorizations in the SorelMontreal sector of the navigational waterway, namely Sorel, Contrecoeur, Varennes, Montreal-Frontenac and Montreal-Jetty No. 1.
In light of the particular features of the navigational waterway in the portion between buoys M84 (downstream of the municipality of Verchères) and M157 (opposite to the Port of Montreal, section 109) as well as the No. 1 Anchorage Pointe-aux-Tremble, it was agreed to adjust upward the available water column by 10 cm in this portion.
The minimum water column in this portion of the navigational waterway as per the Varennes hydrographic station, obtained after adjustment, will be used for the calculation of under-keel clearance.
Monthly Notice to Mariners Eastern Edition 08/22 refers.
                                                    Cancels NW-Q-1353-22
